blocks.text: Thermoset molding is a manufacturing process used to produce precision components from materials that undergo a permanent chemical transformation during curing.

Unlike thermoplastics, which can be reheated and remelted, thermoset materials form a cross-linked molecular structure during the curing process. Once cured, they retain their finished shape and cannot simply be melted and reprocessed.
This process produces components with properties that can include:

items.text: Performance in elevated-temperature environments.
items.label: Heat resistance

items.text: Compatibility with oils, fuels, solvents, and other industrial chemicals.
items.label: Chemical resistance

items.text: Consistent shape and performance under specified operating conditions.
items.label: Dimensional stability

items.text: Dielectric properties in selected thermoset formulations.
items.label: Electrical insulation

items.text: Strength, durability, flexibility, or vibration resistance depending on material selection.
items.label: Mechanical performance

items.text: Engineered performance in repeated-use and demanding service applications.
items.label: Long-term reliability

blocks.text: Thermoset materials include both rigid engineered plastics and flexible elastomers, allowing manufacturers to develop components for a broad range of industrial applications.
SYNC offers multiple manufacturing processes to accommodate different part designs, material requirements, production volumes, and performance specifications.

Compression molding uses heat and pressure to form thermoset materials within a precision mold. A measured amount of material is placed directly into the mold cavity, where it flows and cures into the required geometry.

Compression molding is particularly effective for larger components, industrial rubber products, seals, pads, and applications where material characteristics and tooling economics are important considerations.
Our capabilities include large-format molding, custom rubber components, silicone molding, and rubber-to-metal bonded assemblies.
Transfer molding uses a heated chamber and controlled pressure to move uncured material into a closed mold cavity.
This process is well suited for complex geometries, molded-in inserts, rubber-to-metal bonding, and applications requiring controlled material flow.
SYNC's transfer molding expertise supports both engineered thermoset plastics and elastomeric components.
Thermoset injection molding introduces material into a heated mold, where it undergoes a chemical curing reaction to form the finished component.
The process can be particularly effective for repeat production, intricate features, and applications requiring consistent part geometry and material performance.

Our engineering teams help determine whether injection, compression, or transfer molding provides the most practical solution based on part design, material selection, and anticipated production volume.
Selecting the correct material is critical to long-term component performance. SYNC works with a wide range of engineered thermoset plastics and elastomer compounds.

items.q: What is the difference between thermoset and thermoplastic molding?
a: Thermoset materials undergo a permanent curing reaction that creates a cross-linked molecular structure. Thermoplastics soften when heated and can typically be melted and reformed. The optimal material depends on required temperature resistance, chemical compatibility, mechanical performance, part geometry, and cost.

items.q: What types of products can be manufactured using thermoset molding?
a: Common applications include seals, gaskets, rubber bumpers, vibration isolators, electrical insulators, structural components, molded inserts, and custom industrial parts.

items.q: Which molding process is best for my application?
a: Compression molding, transfer molding, and injection molding offer different advantages. The optimal process depends on component geometry, material selection, tolerances, tooling requirements, and production volume. SYNC can evaluate these factors during the quotation process.

items.q: Can SYNC manufacture rubber-to-metal bonded components?
a: Yes. SYNC offers rubber-to-metal bonding capabilities for applications requiring integrated metal and elastomer components.

items.q: Does SYNC support prototype and production manufacturing?
a: Yes. Our manufacturing teams support product development, prototype requirements, and ongoing production programs, subject to the requirements of the individual component and manufacturing process.
